issue: The text says node denominators divide Gamma_X 2^alpha with alpha = J + O(I) + mu K_mu, 'so they do not grow with the number of stages'. Read literally this is false: alpha contains the stage limit J. What is proved, and what the bound needs, is that one bound holds at every stage of a trial, so denominators do not compound from stage to stage.
evidence: In appendix-growth.tex:119, alpha = J + max_i|e_i| + |E| + mu K_mu. A node is a center plus or minus 2^{E-j-e_i}((2^mu+1)^k - 2^{mu k})/2^{mu(k-1)}, and the numerator is odd. So the 2-adic denominator exponent is up to J + |E| + max|e_i| + mu K_mu, which grows linearly with J. The bound is uniform over the stages j <= J because centers and clipped endpoints are earlier nodes.
fix: growth.tex: replace 'so they do not grow with the number of stages' with 'so one bound holds at all stages of a trial: denominators do not compound from stage to stage'. appendix-growth.tex:129: replace 'So denominators do not grow with the number of stages.' with 'So the bound does not compound from stage to stage; it depends on the stage limit only through the term J in alpha.'

issue: The summary 'under rETH the exponent of kappa cannot be o(p)' omits the qualifier that the polynomial in I has fixed degree. Prop prop:lbproduct only excludes running times f(p)(kappa I)^{p/psi(p)}, in particular f(p)kappa^{a(p)}I^C with C constant.
evidence: On the hard instances both kappa and I are poly(kN_0) (App. G.2, 'Conditioning'), so the reduction cannot separate the exponent of kappa from the degree in I. An algorithm with running time kappa^3 I^p has kappa-exponent 3 = o(p) but is not of the excluded form. It contradicts neither Prop 10.6 nor ETH: it gives N_0^{O(k)} on the clique instances and 2^{O(I)} on the instances of Prop 10.1, where log kappa = O(I). Theorem 1.2(c) and the sentence after Prop 10.6 ('in the sense a(p) <= p/psi(p) above') are precise; the shorthand summaries are not.
fix: limits.tex 21-22: 'under randomized ETH the exponent of $\kappa$ in a bound $f(p)\kappa^{a(p)}I^{O(1)}$ cannot be $o(p)$, already for integer box quadratics (Proposition~\ref{prop:lbproduct})'.
